newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Iscor sees substantially better 2H earnings.
newsitem.headline: Iscor sees substantially better 2H earnings.

text.p: Iron and steel producer Iscor said on Tuesday it expected a substantial improvement in earnings in the second half of its financial year.
The company earlier reported a 66 percent fall in attributable income to 170 million rand in the six months to December 31.

"With production at Vanderbijlpark back to normal together with the benefit of the weaker rand, we expect earnings for the second six months of the year to be substantially better than the previous six months," Iscor executive chairman Hans Smith said.
However, the results for the period to December 31 1996 would prevent it from achieving the 26 cents per share the company had hoped to achieve for the full financial year, he said.
Smith said first half earnings were hit by a seven percent decrease in local steel sales volumes which resulted in local sales dropping to 54 percent from 58 percent in 1995.
"International dollar selling prices for steel decreased on average by 16 percent and together with the increased export tonnages further eroded margins," Smith said.

The recommissioning of relined blast furnace C and continuous caster at Vanderbijlpark Works and the commissioning of Pretoria Stainless Steel had been non-repetitive events that also affected operations negatively.
"On the iron ore export side, volumes decreased by 13 percent due to problems on the Sishen-Saldanha railway line," he said.
Smith said the announcement of the company's results had been brought forward by three weeks to inform shareholders and the market as soon as possible of the poor results.
Iscor annnounced last August that first-half earnings would be substantially lower than in the period to December 1995.
But Smith said on Tuesday: "Trading conditions have been far more difficult than anticipated and that has affected our financial performance."
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell analyst John Loewen said the results were well below market expectations of between eight and 10 cents a share.
"Our understanding is that there is not any one particular factor, just general market weakness that has contributed to these bad results," Loewen said.
Smith said that net cash outflow in the period was 926 million rand compared to 104 million rand in 1995.
"The deterioration resulted from the operational results, increased tax payments of 222 million rand and the increased level of capital expenditure."
Operating income at the company's steel division plunged 65 percent, while its mining division managed a five percent improvement in operating income.
Net financing costs were 51 million rand compared to net interest earned of 43 million rand in the previous period.
Capital expenditure of 855 million rand included costs for the upgrading of Vanderbijlpark Works and the planned replacement of mining equipment.
Loewen said the worse-than-expected results could result in Iscor's share price falling sharply on Wednesday.
"The share could take a smack tomorrow. It could easily come off about 15 percent," Loewen said, adding that some support may be evident around 300 cents.
Iscor shares ended Johannesburg Stock Exchange trade one cent firmer at 3.61 rand on Tuesday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
